modules.label: Dismissive responses and gestures
modules.summary: Moments where gestures or comments dismiss the speaker in front of others.
examples: My manager rolled his eyes when I asked about the budget.
My teenager muttered "whatever" and slammed the bedroom door.
A teammate whispered to another person and laughed after I spoke.

cues.example: At today's 9 a.m. budget review in conference room B, my manager rolled his eyes right after I asked for the spreadsheet update.
My teenager muttered "whatever" and slammed the bedroom door after I asked about homework tonight.
At dinner tonight at Sam's Diner, a friend said "You're too sensitive" when I declined the joke.
During Tuesday's 2 p.m. planning stand-up, my colleague whispered to Taylor and they both laughed right after I described the roadmap change.

modules.label: When listening feels one-sided
modules.summary: Moments where partners or clients talk over you or insist you never listen.
examples: My partner said I never listen when we talked about chores.
During the call, the client talked over every proposal.
The conversation kept looping because my input was interrupted.

cues.example: Yesterday evening in the kitchen, my partner said "You never listen" when we talked about chores.
During this morning's 10 a.m. project video call, the client's audio overlapped mine three times when I proposed a change.

modules.label: Walkouts during presentations
modules.summary: Abandoning the room mid-presentation or slamming notebooks while someone shares.
examples: A coworker slammed her notebook and left during the presentation.
Someone walked out as I showed the final slide.
The room fell silent after the door closed behind them.

cues.example: A coworker slammed her notebook shut and walked out during my presentation yesterday.

modules.label: Missed fouls and officiating gaps
modules.summary: Referees overlooking fouls or making no-calls that impact fairness and safety.
examples: The referee missed three fouls in a row.
No whistle blew when our player was shoved.
The bench kept shouting about the no-call.

cues.example: During last night's game, the referee missed three fouls against our team.

modules.label: Fairness in lines and shared resources
modules.summary: When service staff or shoppers bypass the queue or reach over you for the last item.
examples: The barista served someone who arrived after me.
Another shopper reached over my shoulder for the last carton.
I stayed in line but others jumped ahead.

cues.example: The barista skipped me and served two people who arrived later in line this afternoon.
At the grocery store, another shopper reached over me to grab the last carton of eggs.

modules.label: Shared space upkeep and boundaries
modules.summary: Living with others who leave messes or return shared items without care.
examples: Dishes piled up again in the sink before work.
A borrowed car came back with an empty tank.
Shared chores keep getting skipped.

cues.example: My roommate left dirty dishes piled in the sink again before leaving for work.
My sibling borrowed my car without asking and returned it with the tank empty.

modules.label: Employment status surprises
modules.summary: Contract endings or renewals delivered without context or warning.
examples: HR emailed that my contract wasn't renewed without a reason.
A contract ended without anyone explaining why.
Employment status shifted with no warning.

cues.example: The email from HR said my contract wasn't renewed with no explanation.

modules.label: Feedback without specifics
modules.summary: Critiques that label work as sloppy or list mistakes without examples.
examples: A teacher wrote 'sloppy' across the assignment.
A review listed mistakes without concrete examples.
Feedback lacked specifics about what to adjust.

cues.example: The teacher handed back my child's assignment with "sloppy" written across the top.
I received a performance review that only listed mistakes without any concrete examples.

modules.label: Maintenance requests with no follow-up
modules.summary: Landlords or contractors who ignore repairs or miss appointments without notice.
examples: Messages about the leak went unanswered.
A contractor missed the appointment and never called.
Maintenance issues linger without updates.

cues.example: The landlord hasn't responded to three messages about the leak this week.
The contractor missed today's 8 a.m. appointment and hasn't texted or called.

modules.label: Care visits that feel rushed
modules.summary: Providers who glance at the clock or otherwise signal impatience while you explain symptoms.
examples: The doctor kept checking the clock mid-appointment.
A provider glanced at the clock while I spoke.
The visit felt rushed instead of attentive.

cues.example: My doctor glanced at the clock twice while I was describing my symptoms today.

modules.label: Workload stacking and late-night pings
modules.summary: Teams that hand you every follow-up task or bosses who ping late at night without regard for rest.
examples: All the follow-up tasks landed on my plate again.
Slack pings came in around midnight from my boss.
I keep getting the action items after every meeting.

cues.example: In last Thursday's sprint retrospective, the project lead assigned me every follow-up action item again.
My boss sent me three Slack messages between 11 p.m. and midnight about tomorrow's report.

modules.label: Disconnected dinners
modules.summary: Shared meals where someone stays on their phone instead of engaging.
examples: Phones stayed on the table during dinner.
Conversation faded while someone scrolled.
I looked up and saw them on their screen instead of with me.

cues.example: My partner scrolled through their phone during dinner instead of looking up.

modules.label: Noisy rideshares
modules.summary: Drivers who fill the car with loud speakerphone calls or chatter during the ride.
examples: A driver talked loudly on speakerphone the whole trip.
The car felt like a call center during the ride.
Noise filled the ride instead of quiet.

cues.example: The rideshare driver talked loudly on speakerphone for the entire trip yesterday.

modules.label: Early-morning noise
modules.summary: Neighbors or surroundings that create loud noise before the day starts.
examples: A dog barked for thirty minutes at 6 a.m.
Weekend mornings start with loud barking next door.
Noise woke me up before sunrise.

cues.example: My neighbor's dog barked loudly for 30 minutes starting at 6 a.m. on Saturday.

modules.label: Traffic safety scares
modules.summary: Cyclists or others rushing through red lights where pedestrians cross.
examples: A cyclist ran the red light through the crosswalk.
Bikes sped through while the walk signal was on.
Someone on a bike ignored the traffic signal next to me.

cues.example: A cyclist sped through the crosswalk even though the light was red this morning.

modules.label: Noticing my own delays
modules.summary: Recognizing when you scroll or stall instead of following through on your plans.
examples: I scrolled instead of returning an important call.
An hour went by on my phone before I reached out.
I delayed following through because I kept scrolling.

cues.example: I caught myself scrolling for an hour instead of calling my grandmother back.

modules.label: Teammates catching mistakes before they spread
modules.summary: When coworkers double-check work and spot errors before they reach others.
examples: A teammate double-checked an expense report and caught an error before it went out.
Someone on the team spotted a calculation mistake and flagged it before the client saw it.
A coworker reviewed my draft and found a typo in the headline.

cues.example: My coworker double-checked the expense report and caught a mistake before we sent it.

modules.label: Celebrations of personal milestones
modules.summary: Coaches or teammates who visibly celebrate your progress or new personal bests.
examples: At the 8 a.m. session, the trainer high-fived me after I racked 185 pounds on squats.
The coach paused practice to high-five me when the board showed my new record.
Teammates clapped while the trainer called out the weight I just logged.

cues.example: At the 8 a.m. session, the gym trainer high-fived me right after I racked 185 pounds on squats.

modules.label: Neighbors lending a hand
modules.summary: Neighbors who step in to clear a path or help with home care while you are away.
examples: A neighbor shoveled our sidewalk while we were gone.
Someone next door cleared the driveway before we got home.
Our neighbor salted the steps so we wouldn't slip.

cues.example: My neighbor shoveled our sidewalk after the snowstorm while we were at work.

modules.label: Specific appreciation and thank-yous
modules.summary: Heartfelt notes or emails that name what you contributed and why it mattered.
examples: At 4 p.m., the coordinator emailed naming the volunteer shifts I covered on Saturday.
The principal highlighted the exact stations I staffed during the fundraiser.
A manager DM’d the timestamps where I stepped in during the launch.

cues.example: At 4 p.m., the coordinator emailed me listing the volunteer shifts I covered during the fundraiser.

modules.label: Reflective listening during support sessions
modules.summary: Counselors or listeners who mirror your words before offering input so you feel heard.
examples: A therapist reflected my words before sharing ideas.
A counselor paused to mirror back what I said.
A support group facilitator summarized my message first.

cues.example: During therapy, my counselor paused and reflected back exactly what I said before offering input.

modules.label: Loved ones and leads sharing the load
modules.summary: Partners or managers who redistribute tasks so responsibilities feel shared.
examples: My partner handled dinner and dishes so I could finish a deadline.
During Monday's sprint review, the project manager assigned two follow-up tasks to each teammate.
A friend swapped shifts so we split the weekend coverage.

cues.example: My partner cooked dinner and cleaned the kitchen while I finished my deadline.
During Monday's sprint review, the project manager assigned two follow-up tasks to each teammate.

modules.label: Strangers returning lost items intact
modules.summary: Moments when someone brings back what you dropped with nothing missing.
examples: Outside the market at 3 p.m., a stranger handed back my wallet with the cash still inside.
Security called me to pick up my phone after a customer turned it in at the front desk.
A passerby jogged over with the keys I dropped on the sidewalk.

cues.example: Outside the market at 3 p.m., a stranger handed back my wallet with the cash still inside the billfold.

modules.label: Quick responses to time-off requests
modules.summary: Leaders who respond promptly when you ask for time away from work.
examples: My manager approved my vacation request the same day.
HR confirmed my PTO within a few hours.
A supervisor okayed my time off without delay.

cues.example: My boss approved my vacation request the same day I submitted it.

modules.label: Care teams offering calm, attentive updates
modules.summary: Medical staff who explain steps or check in to reassure you and your loved ones.
examples: A nurse checked in overnight to make sure my dad was comfortable.
A dentist explained each step before starting the procedure.
A tech walked us through the test process in advance.

cues.example: The nurse checked in twice during the night to make sure my dad was comfortable.
My dentist explained each step before starting the procedure.

modules.label: Deliveries marked complete with nothing there
modules.summary: Orders showing as delivered when no package actually arrived.
examples: At 7 p.m. the app marked my dinner order delivered while the porch camera still showed an empty doorstep.
The tracker pinged "delivered" even though the hallway camera never recorded a drop-off.
Courier status flipped to delivered, but the lobby shelf stayed empty all night.

cues.example: At 7 p.m. the delivery app marked my order as delivered while the porch camera still showed an empty doorstep.

modules.label: Late arrivals without notice
modules.summary: Friends or contacts who show up far past the meeting time without sending a heads-up.
examples: A friend arrived half an hour late with no text.
Someone showed up late to lunch without a heads-up.
My date was 30 minutes late and never messaged.

cues.example: My friend arrived 30 minutes late to lunch without texting.

modules.label: Unexpected policy warning letters
modules.summary: Associations or boards that send a warning without first talking it through.
examples: The HOA sent a lawn warning letter without asking first.
A board left a notice about hedge height with no conversation.
Management posted a warning about patio chairs without talking to us.

cues.example: Our HOA sent a warning letter about lawn length without asking first.

modules.label: Credit given to the wrong person
modules.summary: Moments when someone else claims your idea or contribution in front of others.
examples: A colleague took credit for my idea in the pitch.
Someone presented my work as theirs during the meeting.
An editor left my name off the project summary.

cues.example: My colleague took credit for my idea during the pitch meeting.

modules.label: Care teams that miss critical updates
modules.summary: Childcare or health providers who forget to call about urgent symptoms.
examples: Daycare forgot to call when my child had a fever.
The clinic didn't phone about a concerning result.
Camp missed letting us know about an injury.

cues.example: The daycare forgot to call when my child had a fever.

modules.label: Transit drivers who wait for you
modules.summary: Drivers who pause the route so you can catch up and ride.
examples: A bus driver waited as I ran toward the stop.
The train conductor held the doors when I called out.
A shuttle driver paused so I could board.

cues.example: The bus driver waited for me when I was running toward the stop.

modules.label: Team updates that go missing
modules.summary: Moments when teammates skip shared boards or updates for days at a time.
examples: From Monday through Friday, no cards under Jordan's initials moved on the shared sprint board.
The kanban view shows five tasks assigned to Sam untouched since last Tuesday.
Our tracker still lists Casey's items in "In Progress" after a full week.

cues.example: From Monday through Friday, no cards under my teammate's initials moved on the shared sprint board.

modules.label: Repairs handled right away
modules.summary: Landlords or maintenance crews who respond quickly to repair requests.
examples: Maintenance fixed the leak the day after we reported it.
Our landlord scheduled a plumber the next morning.
The repair team showed up within 24 hours.

cues.example: Our landlord repaired the leaky faucet the day after we reported it.

modules.label: When repayment promises slip
modules.summary: Friends or relatives who miss the payback they said was coming soon.
examples: A sibling missed the repayment they promised Friday.
A friend still hasn't paid me back after saying they would.
Someone delayed sending the money again.

cues.example: My sibling promised to pay me back Friday but still hasn't sent anything.

modules.label: Allergy instructions ignored
modules.summary: Restaurants that serve allergens even after you clearly note them.
examples: The restaurant served my meal with peanuts after I flagged my allergy.
Catering included dairy even though I mentioned the allergy.
A cafe added walnuts despite my warning.

cues.example: The restaurant served my meal with peanuts after I noted my allergy.

modules.label: Meetings scheduled over breaks
modules.summary: Managers who drop meetings onto your lunch or rest time without asking.
examples: My manager scheduled a meeting over my lunch break without asking.
A lead booked a call during my only break.
Someone added a meeting right over my dinner time.

cues.example: My manager scheduled a meeting over my lunch break without asking.

modules.label: Support staff who follow up
modules.summary: Helpers who guide you through a fix and check back afterward.
examples: Yesterday the service agent stayed on the call for each troubleshooting step and emailed this morning to confirm the fix.
IT kept the remote session open until the app loaded and sent a ticket update at 9 a.m.
Customer service called back the next day after guiding me through the reset.

cues.example: Yesterday the service agent stayed on the call for each troubleshooting step and emailed this morning to confirm the fix.

modules.label: City fixes after persistent outreach
modules.summary: Public works teams that finally resolve an issue after repeated contact.
examples: The city fixed the streetlight after months of emails.
Public works repaired the pothole we kept reporting.
The utilities crew finally addressed the outage after persistent follow-up.

cues.example: The city finally fixed the streetlight after months of emails.
